tower-of-hanoi.title: Goal Stack Ordering
tower-of-hanoi.principle: The final configuration on the goal peg must be a descending stack: the largest disk at the bottom and each subsequent disk smaller than the one below it. This ordering guarantees a legal final state.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When checking whether the goal state has been reached or when planning the final arrangement of disks on the target peg.
tower-of-hanoi.example: For 5 disks the goal stack on peg 2 should be [5,4,3,2,1] from bottom to top.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Free Blocked Disk
tower-of-hanoi.principle: A disk that has any smaller disks on top cannot be moved directly; those smaller disks must be relocated first, typically using the auxiliary peg.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Whenever the disk you need to move is not the topmost disk on its peg.
tower-of-hanoi.example: If disk 4 sits under disk 2 on a peg, move disk 2 elsewhere before moving disk 4.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Use Auxiliary Peg for Temporary Storage
tower-of-hanoi.principle: In a three‑peg problem, the peg that is neither the source nor the destination can serve as temporary storage for disks while larger disks are moved.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Whenever you need to clear a peg or hold smaller disks while moving a larger one.
tower-of-hanoi.example: While moving disk 5 from peg 1 to peg 2, use peg 0 to hold disks 1‑4 temporarily.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Check Move Legality
tower-of-hanoi.principle: A legal move must take the topmost disk from the source peg and place it onto a destination peg that is empty or whose top disk is larger than the moving disk.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Before committing any move in the sequence.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Moving disk 3 onto a peg whose top disk is 2 is illegal because 3 > 2.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Simulate Final Configuration
tower-of-hanoi.principle: After constructing a move list, mentally replay each move from the initial state to ensure that every move is legal and that the final configuration matches the goal.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: After writing the complete move sequence, before submitting the answer.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Step through the moves to verify that peg 2 ends with [5,4,3,2,1].

tower-of-hanoi.title: Maintain 0‑Indexed Peg Numbers
tower-of-hanoi.principle: The output format expects peg identifiers 0, 1, 2; using any other numbering (e.g., 1‑based) will cause the verifier to reject the answer.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When writing each move in the answer list.
tower-of-hanoi.example: To move a disk from the first peg to the third, write [disk, 0, 2] not [disk, 1, 3].

tower-of-hanoi.title: Track Current Top Disk on Each Peg
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Keep an up‑to‑date record of the topmost disk on every peg after each move, so you know which disks are movable and which moves are legal.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Throughout the planning and execution of the move sequence.
tower-of-hanoi.example: After moving disk 1 from peg 2 to peg 0, update the top of peg 2 to disk 2.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Leverage Existing Larger Disks on Target as Base
tower-of-hanoi.principle: If the goal peg already contains larger disks that are correctly placed, you can place a smaller disk onto it, building the final stack from bottom up.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When a larger disk has already been positioned on the target peg and you need to add the next smaller disk.
tower-of-hanoi.example: After placing disk 5 on peg 2, you can place disk 4 onto peg 2 because 5 > 4.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Clear Destination Peg of Smaller Top Disk Before Placing Larger Disk
tower-of-hanoi.principle: If the destination peg’s top disk is smaller than the disk you intend to move, you must first relocate that smaller disk (often using the auxiliary peg) before moving the larger disk.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Whenever a move would place a larger disk onto a smaller one.
tower-of-hanoi.example: To move disk 4 onto peg 2 whose top is disk 2, first move disk 2 elsewhere.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Use Smallest Disk as Flexible Buffer
tower-of-hanoi.principle: The smallest disk can be moved onto any peg without violating ordering, making it an ideal temporary buffer for enabling moves of larger disks.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When you need a free peg or to temporarily hold a disk while rearranging larger disks.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Move disk 1 to an empty peg to free up the source peg for moving disk 2.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Placing a larger disk onto a smaller one
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model may forget the fundamental rule that a larger disk cannot rest on a smaller disk.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Always compare the sizes before moving; ensure the destination peg is empty or its top disk is larger than the moving disk.

tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model might assume any disk can be moved regardless of its position on the peg.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Track the topmost disk on each peg and only move that disk.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Prematurely placing a small disk on the goal peg
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model may try to fill the goal peg early, breaking the required descending order later.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Build the goal stack from largest to smallest; only place a smaller disk after all larger disks are correctly positioned.

tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model may default to 1‑based indexing instead of the required 0‑based indexing.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Remember that pegs are numbered 0, 1, 2 in the output format.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Skipping final verification of the goal state
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model may assume the move list is correct without checking the final configuration.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Simulate the entire move sequence and confirm the final configuration matches the goal before submitting.
